India knew they still had to bowl out of their skins if they were to win the Test. Tom Latham copped up a dreadful Test with a pair, Henry Nicholls was taken out by the impressive Prasidh Krishna and they entered Day 5 with the task of getting 8 wickets. They took out both overnight batters, Devon Conway (65) and Rachin Ravindra (37), briefly raising hopes. The wicket of Tom Blundell followed almost immediately after lunch, but then they ran into Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips. On a pitch that remained benign, India tried hard, rotated their pacers, and Sundar bowled a long spell, but they simply couldn't get past the resolute defence of the two batters. The visitors will probably look at the missed chances - none easier than Akash Deep's botched run-out chance to get rid of Mitchell - but they'll agree that they just had no answers to the flatness of the surface. Presentations coming up shortly..

Nicholls (2/2): [Continued your love affair with the Basin Reserve. What is it about this ground that you love?] Yeah, I'm not too sure really. It's nice when you come to a ground that you've had success at. But again, I think when you come here, we expect to look the way it did in the first day. And I think even though it did change and play different to as previously, again, there were still challenges there that we had to negate throughout. And I think that's the most pleasing thing for the group was we managed to find ways to do that. [What are you expecting in Christchurch, you are local boy?] Yeah, it'll be interesting. Again, it's a surface we usually see a bit of grass, a bit of pace. And, hopefully that's the case. But obviously it sets up now for an exciting last game.

Shubman Gill (1/2): [A tough day in the field] No, not really. I think we knew it's gonna be, it's gonna be a challenge to get ten wickets on that wicket. But I think we had our chances, couple of chances here and there with, with the tail you never quite really (know). So I think we had a decent day in the field. [Overall impressed with how you played throughout the test, the bowling innings and the first innings. And then obviously that mammoth batting innings?] Yeah, definitely. I think we were quite impressive. I think touring away from home. And I think we challenged them in all the areas. And that was our, that was the important thing for us even when we came with the ball in the first innings. I think we did decently well. And then obviously with the bat, everyone chipped in, only two hundreds but then we got almost 700 runs, which is a lot.

Latham (3/3): [And how important for the bowling group then to get that day off today? I guess they get one more day than the Indians do leading into Christchurch] Yeah, I guess we sort of spoke about that. Let's say we're only going to bowl once rather than bowling two innings. But yeah, as I said, they were fantastic. They kept charging in, kept trying to beat through as much as they could. We tried to adapt to that wicket, bring the stumps into play a little bit more than probably what we usually do here. But yeah, nice for them to hopefully put their feet up over the next couple of days and get themselves right for Hagley.

That's now two Tests in a row that India have failed to close out. They needed four wickets against Sri Lanka in their previous outing but couldn't get them. Here, they came into the final day needing eight and managed just three. That's 16 WTC points missed across the two drawn Tests. Were flat pitches the only reason, or were there tactical calls that India could have got better? As far as bowling changes were concerned, Gill got most things right. He kept Washington going from one end while rotating the pacers in short bursts from the other. However, the field placements could have been more attacking. India had plenty of runs in the bank and could have afforded to push a few more fielders into catching positions. That was particularly evident when there was no short leg in place for Prasidh, and a chance to dismiss Mitchell went begging. These are the moments India will look back on and wonder what might have been as they head to Christchurch for the second Test.
